label: artmerge6-pb-n3
_why: THE CENTURY n=3 OF THE CRAFTS + MERGES ARM WITH THE SHOPKEEPER CRAFTS (BALANCE_FRAMEWORK §10.91.4). The user, 2026-10-01: "No machinists as artisans. Rather, make them all shopkeepers + labourers ... Once that is decided, we will run a short 10-year probe to check basic health, and if everything is fine, go through with the n=3"; then "30% it is". The 10-year probe (20260930_225621, FINDINGS F191) was healthy: no dead industry, no token market against the canon, the crafts better staffed, world GDP in the canon range. Book config/mod_config.artmerge6-pb.json = artmerge6-floor (the crafts, the merges, the hiring floor; §10.91.1-3) with every craft staffed 30% shopkeepers / 70% laborers and craft output x1.10 food / x1.30 glass / x1.20 tooling / x1.20 paper. A FIXED n=3 as the user named it: every run plays to 1936 whatever the register reads (no stop watcher). The first century reading of the combined book; the user decides after the arc whether both lines are canonised or both go.

_arms.artmerge6-pb: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.artmerge6-pb.json} (+ tech_tree_options.artmerge6-pb.json = the canon tree). Proven by field diff against artmerge6-floor: the six crafts employment, four output_qty and the derived wage_pct / target_be only.

_delta: Against the canon (config/mod_config.json = canon-dams-family-nolog): (1) food/textile/furniture/glass/tooling/paper e0 = craft rungs - per 500-head level 3.6 grain -> 3.71 groceries, 1.95 fabric -> 1.95 clothes, 1.38 wood + 0.46 fabric -> 2.0 furniture, 1.59 wood -> 1.72 glass, 2.23 wood -> 1.91 tools, 3.06 wood -> 2.92 paper; staffing 30% shopkeepers / 70% laborers (§10.91.4); cost 12 (food, paper) or 6; no x1.2 input lift; group bg_pmr_crafts (no economy of scale, urbanization 2, infrastructure x1/10, the hiring floor 0.01); 1836 levels x10 with the pops re-typed; no company builds or forms off them. (2) food e2, textile e3, furniture e3, paper e2, fertilizer e1, steel e3 = methods of the rung below (method_of), hosts at the geometric-midpoint cost and ai_value. e1-e3 of the six craft industries are the canon's (§10.91.1 ruling 1) apart from the merge hosts' cost and ai_value. The canon's measured reference F177 is canon-dams-family = the canon + its monthly dam log (log only).
_comparison: canon-dams-family-n6 (20260929_002728, F177: 4 intact / 1 stall / 1 runoff, consensus loss 5.90; world GDP 0.56 / 1.03 / 1.23 / 1.75 / 1.09 / 0.93) and the pinned vanilla n=16 (20260821_131149). Same dump dates, tags, metrics and quarterly autosaves as F177, so its readers and row P compare directly.

_predictions.gdp: world GDP at the end state 0.95-1.15x vanilla (point ~1.05; the canon's intact 0.93-1.23, consensus 1.06). The crafts ran 0.94-1.02x the canon's median to 1866 and the merges 1.00-1.07x (F184, one seed each); the floor moved nothing outside the crafts in ten years (F188). By the end state the industrial core has no crafts (Britain held 1 craft level at 1866, F184 §3), so the century is carried by e1-e3 = the canon's plus the merges' earlier adoption.
_predictions.crafts: craft WORKERS world-wide peak before 1880 and fall decade over decade after; Britain, France, the USA and Prussia under 5% of their 1836 craft levels by 1880; the periphery (China, India, Russia, the Ottomans) keeps crafts to 1900 and loses most by 1936. FALSIFIED if a shortlist member's craft rung still grows at 1900. Textile's craft out-earned its own e1 in margin at 1845 (F189 §4): if it still does at 1880 in a shortlist market, the old rung is not dying there.
_predictions.labour: pool W 0.80-0.95 (canon 0.88), pool U* 1.0-1.4x (canon 1.18), world W 0.68-0.80 (canon 0.73). T0 / rest 0.005-0.03 (canon 0.015; the pool's crafts die early), T0 1935 / the 1900s under 0.6 (canon 0.39); world T0 above the canon's through 1900 (the crafts hold more people than the canon's e0 in furniture and glass, F189 §4).
_predictions.prices: PI 0.90-1.00 (canon 0.96), PP 0.82-0.95 (canon 0.88); craft goods dearer than the canon's in the craft-holding markets through the 1850s (F184 §5), converging after.
_predictions.merges: Baking Powder adopted from the mid-1840s and Bleached Paper from the mid-1850s in the leaders (F184 §6); the three e3 merges (electric sewing, spray finishing, electric arc: game-era-5 technologies) from ~1905-1920, switching hosts in place (merge_methods.mjs).
_predictions.hard: the canon's two failure modes are inherited unchanged - the stuck Britain (F166, ~1 run in 5-6) and Britain's capital abundance (the canon's run 4) - so 1 broken run in 2-3 would be the canon's own rate, not the arm's fault. An early People's Springtime (before 1843) in a seed would support F184's plausible craft channel (radicals, peasant wealth); the canon's six ran 1843-1845.
_predictions.perf: row P: total play within +10% of the canon's per-run median (F177: 144-185 min with quarterly saves); the craft book's thirty years ran 42.2 min against the canon's 36.9-39.9 on one seed (+8%) while the floor probe's first decade matched the canon's (11.7 min against 11.7-12.4) - watch the mid-century.
_predictions.pb: the Petite Bourgeoisie clout (summary v13 per country, ig_clout.mjs on kept saves) about 0.3 points above the machinist crafts world mean through the crafts life (F191), fading as the crafts die; readable against the canon only through the 1926-1936 trend of its kept end saves

_register: Read with criteria.mjs --arm <session>:artmerge6-pb (the book comes from build_state.json), alignment_check.mjs for the F114 divergence test, and the craft readers (craft_fill.mjs, hiring_census.mjs, labour_flows.mjs, construction_spend.mjs --mod <the built arm>, merge_methods.mjs, rung_econ.mjs - which counts a craft level as 500 heads since 2026-09-30). Expected consensus loss inside the canon's per-run spread (its intact runs 5.3 / 7.0 / 7.8 / 8.0; consensus 5.90). Statistics are DIRECTIONAL (§10.83.7): the verdict weighs mechanisms, not a two-book loss gap. The decision is the user's: canonise both lines or drop both, after the arc.
_stop_rule: FIXED n=3 (the user named n=3): no stop watcher, all three runs play to 1936 whatever the register reads; the register still grades each run (hard breaks reported as broken runs) and the consensus is read from the intact ones.
_cost: 3 runs x 1836 -> 1936, about 2.5-3 h each (F177: 144-185 min with quarterly saves), about 8-9 h
